title: Synonym precision
summary: Distinguish near-synonyms by their core meaning, degree and emotional colouring before testing the best fit in a complete sentence.

sections.title: Close in meaning is not identical
content: Compare ‘a narrow path’, ‘a thin sheet’ and ‘a cramped room’. All three suggest limited space, but each describes a different kind of limitation. A familiar general meaning is only the start of a synonym decision.
For each candidate, ask what it describes exactly, how strong it is and what attitude it carries. Then test it in the complete sentence.

sections.title: Use Core, Degree, Attitude and Sentence
content: Core: state the exact person, action, quality or condition named in the sentence. Words can overlap generally while pointing to different features.
Degree: place the intended meaning on a scale. Warm, hot and scorching all concern heat, but they do not make the same claim.
Attitude: check whether the word sounds approving, neutral or critical. Assertive can praise clear confidence; aggressive suggests harmful force.
Sentence: substitute the candidate and reread all the evidence. Reject a word that changes the fact, exaggerates the degree or adds an unsupported judgement.

sections.title: Separate persistence from stubbornness
content: Consider: ‘After two designs failed, Laila tested a third and changed it when her partner identified a weakness.’ The core idea is continued effort. The revisions show flexibility and response to evidence.

Persistent fits that evidence. Stubborn also suggests continued action, but adds an unwillingness to change; the sentence shows the opposite. Determined is possible in some contexts, but persistent most precisely highlights continuing after repeated difficulty.
The best synonym is not simply the nearest dictionary neighbour. It preserves the exact evidence and does not import an attitude the sentence cannot support.

sections.title: Name the deciding difference
content: For two items, eliminate each option by naming the failed dimension: wrong core meaning, wrong degree or wrong attitude. Point to the words in the sentence that settle the choice.

sections.title: Predict before comparing options
content: On three unseen items, write a short prediction such as ‘confident but respectful’, ‘small in seriousness’ or ‘brief without losing essential meaning’. Compare the options only after the prediction is clear.
Choose the narrowest claim supported by the sentence. Do not reward dramatic or impressive-sounding vocabulary when the evidence supports a more measured word.

sections.title: Diagnose the meaning shift
content: Core-meaning drift: the option belongs to the same broad topic but names a different feature. Degree shift: it makes the claim too weak or too strong. Attitude shift: it adds praise or criticism not supported by the sentence. Familiarity trap: it was selected because it was known, not because it was precise.
Record the earliest failed check and repair the answer with one contrast: ‘X fits because ..., whereas Y would imply ...’.

sections.title: Transfer the precision check
content: Complete one unseen near-synonym decision without a labelled dimension. A failed or hinted attempt enters the retry queue with a fresh context and a different synonym set rather than repeating the exposed answer.
